Unsaturated α‑Ketoesters with Allenyl Boronate Regulated by Chiral

ABSTRACT: A method for asymmetric propargylation and allenylation of β,γ-
unsaturated α-ketoesters catalyzed by Box-Cu/Box-Zn using a commercial organo-
boron reagent is reported. The reaction was demonstrated to be broadly tolerant of
functional groups, resulting in a series of propargyl and allenyl tertiary alcohols in
excellent yields with high enantio- and regioselectivities. Furthermore, the proposed
mechanism was supported by density functional theory calculations. Gram-scale
experiments as well as the synthesis of various chiral tertiary alcohols and glycol
derivatives demonstrated the practicality of this synthetic strategy.
H
omopropargyl and allenyl alcohols are common motifs
in biologically active natural products and pharmaceut-
ical compounds as well as essential synthetic units.
1
Although
numerous methodologies for synthesizing these alcohols exist,
the most straightforward and effective method remains the
addition of propargyl or allenyl reagents to carbonyl
compounds. Chiral secondary homopropargyl and allenyl
alcohols have been successfully synthesized through the
addition of various propargyl and allenyl metal species (Sn-,
Zn-, B-, Si-, or In-based) to aldehydes, respectively.
2
However,
the synthesis of chiral tertiary homopropargyl and allenyl
alcohols has received less attention due to the inferior activity
and selectivity of ketones compared to aldehydes. This study
mainly focuses on highly active ketones, such as fluoro-
substituted ketones,
3
isatins,
4
and methyl ketones.
5
Allenylboronic acid pinacol ester is commercially available
and relatively stable, which has been widely used for
enantioselective propargylation and allenylation of ketones to
synthesize homopropargyl tertiary alcohols in recent year-
s.
3a,b,4a−d,5a,b
However, allenylmetals can undergo a metal-
lotropic rearrangement resulting in either homopropargyl
alcohol or allenyl alcohol when reacting with a carbonyl
compound in a metal-catalyzed system,
6
as a metal−boron
exchange reaction occurs between allenylboronic acid pinacol
ester and the metal catalyst. Nevertheless, selectively synthesiz-
ing chiral homopropargyl or allenyl alcohols by controlling
metallotropic rearrangement remains challenging.
The Fandrick group obtained racemic allenyl alcohols with
high selectivity (93:7 to 99:1 allenyl:alkynyl) by zinc-catalyzed
allenylations of aldehydes and ketones.
7
Subsequently, a
practical and highly site-selective allenylation with propargyl
boronates was developed. Site selectivity can be guided by BPE
ligands and boronate substituents, with high selectivity
(≤99:1) obtained with either propargyl or allenyl adducts
(Scheme 1A).
8
However, the enantioselectivities of the
propargyl and allenyl adducts were not studied. In 2015, the
Kobayashi group synthesized racemic tertiary allenyl and
homopropargyl alcohols with high selectivities from the same
starting materials simply by altering the zinc reagent loading. In
addition, a catalytic asymmetric variant of the allenylation of
ketoesters was conducted, but only tertiary allenyl alcohol with
68% ee was obtained through allenylation of ketoesters
(Scheme 1B).
9
Jarvo et al. developed silver-catalyzed addition
reactions of allenylboronic acid pinacol esters to ketoesters to
provide homopropargyl alcohols with excellent enantioselec-
tivity, but accompanied by poor regioselectivity (2.5:1
homopropargyl:allenyl) (Scheme 1C).
10
Therefore, using
readily available allenylboronic acid pinacol ester and
ketoesters to highly selectively synthesize optically active
tertiary homopropargyl and allenyl alcohols by controlling the
metallotropic rearrangement remains a challenge.
Herein, we carried out the reaction between allenylboronic
acid pinacol ester and β,γ-unsaturated α-ketoesters under mild
conditions and obtained tertiary homopropargyl and allenyl
alcohols with high enantioselectivity and regioselectivity by
adjusting the metal reagent and solvent, respectively (Scheme
1D).
To assess the feasibility of the reaction, we initiated the
identification of the reaction parameters using 2a with 3 as
prototype substrates with copper catalysts. In the presence of

With the optimal reaction conditions in hand, various β,γ-
unsaturated α-ketoesters were investigated to study the
application scope of the developed methodology (Table 2).
In these examples, all reactions afforded chiral homopropargyl
tertiary alcohols (4a−4q) with high enantioselectivity and
good regioselectivity for propargylation over allenylation. A
range of functional groups and substitution patterns were
tolerated. The substitution of R
2

with large steric hindrance generated homopropargyl products

enantioselectivities, and excellent regioselectivities, suggesting

this reaction system. Except for 4g, 4o, and 4q, homopropargyl
alcohols 4d−4p had good yields, which might be due to the
generation of byproducts caused by the alcohol trans-
esterification of unsaturated ketoesters and isopropanol.
Then, we expanded the tolerance of alkynyl ketoesters with
various substituents in this reaction system. The results
indicated that 4aa−4ah exhibited high enantioselectivity and
excellent regioselectivity. Notably, although moderate yields

catalyzed homopropylation to the multistep synthesis of

the corresponding homopropargyl alcohol, whereas the alkyl-
substituted glyoxylate gave 4aj with high enantioselectivity and
excellent regioselectivity. In the process, the absolute
configuration of 4l was determined to be R by X-ray.
We subsequently expanded the substrates for the asym-
metric synthesis of tertiary allenyl alcohols with zinc catalysts
(Table 3). A wide range of substrates bearing strong steric
hindrance (5b and 5c), both electron-donating groups (5d−
5g, 5ab, and 5ac), halogenated (5h−5l and 5ad−5af),
heteroaryl (5o and 5p), β-naphthyl (5q and 5ag), styryl
(5r), 4-biphenyl (5s and 5ah), and aliphatic groups (5ai), can
participate in the reaction. The desired tertiary allenyl alcohols
were constructed in 78−99% yields with 66−96% ee. Good
regioselectivity was obtained for all products, except 5o, 5r,
and 5ai. Aryl-substituted glyoxylate cannot produce allenyl
alcohol, while alkyl-substituted glyoxylate can afford 5aj with
high enantioselectivity and good regioselectivity. 4l was
reduced to give highly enantioselective 4ak, and 5l was
reduced by the same method; its reduction product was
determined by HPLC to be highly enantioselective, and the
times of the major and minor peaks are consistent with 4ak.
Therefore, the configuration of 5l was determined to be R.

In summary, an asymmetric propargylation and allenylation
of β,γ-unsaturated α-ketoesters with a commercial organo-
boron reagent was developed under Box-Cu/Box-Zn catalysis.
A series of unsaturated allenylation and allenyl tertiary alcohols
were afforded in excellent yields with high enantio- and
regioselectivities. The proposed mechanism was supported by
a density functional theory (DFT) calculation. The synthetic
utility of this strategy was demonstrated by gram-scale
experiments and the synthesis of various chiral tertiary alcohol
and glycol derivatives.

ABSTRACT: A method for asymmetric propargylation and allenylation of
\beta , \gamma \mathrm { . }
unsaturated α-ketoesters catalyzed by Box-Cu/Box-Zn using a commercial organo-
boron reagent is reported. The reaction was demonstrated to be broadly tolerant of
functional groups, resulting in a series of propargyl and allenyl tertiary alcohols in
excellent yields with high enantio- and regioselectivities. Furthermore, the proposed
mechanism was supported by density functional theory calculations. Gram-scale
experiments as well as the synthesis of various chiral tertiary alcohols and glycol
derivatives demonstrated the practicality of this synthetic strategy.

In summary, an asymmetric propargylation and allenylation
of β,γ-unsaturated α-ketoesters with a commercial organo-
boron reagent was developed under Box-Cu/Box-Zn catalysis.
A series of unsaturated allenylation and allenyl tertiary alcohols
were aforded in excellent yields with high enantio- and
regioselectivities. The proposed mechanism was supported by
a density functional theory (DFT) calculation. The synthetic
utility of this strategy was demonstrated by gram-scale
experiments and the synthesis of various chiral tertiary alcohol
and glycol derivatives.
